title: Why Fear the Fear of Failure? – Imperatives for Refining our Education System
what_it_is: Why Fear the Fear of Failure? – Imperatives for Refining our Education System

sections.label: PISA fear of failure
sections.summary: PISA found 78% of Singapore students doubt their future plans when failing, and 72% worry what others think.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The PISA test introduced a new measure to assess students’ fear of failure where compared to students from other countries, we have the highest percentage of students, 78%, agreeing or strongly agreeing with the phrase, "When I am failing, this makes me doubt my plans for the future".

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Tellingly, 72% of Singapore students also worry about what others would think of them if they fail, reflecting the resounding weight of failure on their sense of self-worth.

sections.label: Removing exams and rankings
sections.summary: Mid-year exams for certain primary and secondary levels are scrapped, and report books no longer show rankings or decimal marks.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mid-year examinations for Primary 3 and Primary 5 and Secondary 1 and Secondary 3 students are being progressively scrapped, and all graded assessments and examinations at Primary 1 and Primary 2 have also been removed to give young pupils two test-free years.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Report books no longer state the class and level rankings of primary and secondary school students, and marks for each subject are rounded off and presented as whole numbers, without decimal points, to minimise the intense focus on marks.

sections.label: Assignment score statistics
sections.summary: Some would include highest, lowest and median assignment scores so pupils can see where they stand relative to others.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some would also include the highest, lowest and median scores for the assignments, thereby allowing pupils to place where they stood relative to everyone else.

sections.label: Consistent focus away from grades
sections.summary: Reducing excessive focus on grades must be practised consistently across the board, including teacher-parent communication.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Fundamentally, if we want to reduce the excessive focus on grades in our education system, we must ensure that this is practised consistently and across the board, not just in report books but also in everyday teacher-parent communication.

sections.label: Online release of results
sections.summary: Universities and polytechnics already release results online, and PSLE, O, A level and IB results could be released online privately.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As it stands, our universities and polytechnics already successfully release their exam results online.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am confident that with our Smart Nation infrastructure, that we can well handle the online release of PSLE, GCE "O", "A" level and IB results that allow students and their families to receive and process the information in the privacy of their own homes.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For students who wish to seek support after the results, schools can be open for the day to welcome whoever wishes to consult, commiserate or even celebrate with teachers.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But give all students the option of receiving their results privately.

sections.label: Fear of failure impedes growth
sections.summary: Fear of failure makes people conservative and can impede personal growth, creativity and innovation needed in an unpredictable world.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When we fear failure, we tend to be more conservative, stick to the tried and tested, and hesitate to venture into new territory.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The fear of failure can, therefore, impede personal growth, creativity and innovation, all of which are critical assets for our young people as they mature in a future that is promising, but also challenging.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the ongoing coronavirus crisis sharply demonstrates, ours is a decidedly unpredictable world where curve balls abound.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If our young people are crippled by the fear of failure, and do not nurture a growth mindset that is open to constant adaptation, they will find it difficult to manage change and uncertainty.

sections.label: Stopped announcing top PSLE scorers
sections.summary: Announcing top PSLE scorers and secondary school academic banding was stopped to avoid undue pressure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To avoid undue pressure, we had stopped announcing the top PSLE scorer and the academic banding of secondary schools.

sections.label: Setbacks and aptitude-based admissions
sections.summary: Temporary setbacks do not curtail future educational opportunities, and DSA and aptitude-based admissions exist for secondary schools, JCs and IHLs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As a result, experiencing temporary setbacks certainly does not curtail future opportunities in their educational journey, nor does it equate to being a failure in life.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We have introduced Direct School Admission (DSA) to our secondary schools and JCs, and different forms of aptitude-based admissions for our institutes of higher learning (IHLs).

sections.label: Full Subject-Based Banding pilot
sections.summary: The Full Subject-Based Banding pilot has started in secondary schools, moving away from stream labels so students are less likely to limit themselves.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In secondary schools, the pilot for Full Subject-Based Banding (Full SBB) has started.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This marks our move away from stream labels, so that students are less likely to impose a self-limiting mindset on themselves.

sections.label: NITEC students upgrading by 2030
sections.summary: By 2030, all NITEC students will have the opportunity to upgrade to a Higher NITEC and progress through work-study diplomas or full-time programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: By 2030, all National Institute of Technical Education Certificate (NITEC) students will have the opportunity to upgrade to a Higher NITEC over the course of their careers and can progress further through work-study diplomas or full-time programmes.

sections.label: Student's work-study entrepreneurship programme
sections.summary: While pursuing a Diploma in Advertising and Public Relations, he used a work-study entrepreneurship programme in Jakarta and a $5,000 Kickstarter grant to launch his company.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: While pursuing his Diploma in Advertising and Public Relations, he took advantage of the school's work-study entrepreneurship programme in Jakarta, a $5,000 Kickstarter grant, and with his parents' blessings, eventually launched his company three years ago, which now boasts an international client base.

sections.label: Redefining success and failure
sections.summary: Parents and families have a part to play, and society should redefine how it measures success and reacts to failure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: At the same time, parents and families also have a part to play.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We, as a society, should also start to redefine how we measure success and react to failure.

sections.label: Checking results online option
sections.summary: A Member asks whether the Ministry is open to exploring giving all students the choice of checking their results online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Prof Lim Sun Sun, you have no right of reply.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun
sentences.text: I just wanted to ask if the Ministry was open to even exploring the option of giving all students the choice of checking their results online.

sections.label: Reviewing results release support system
sections.summary: The Ministry continuously reviews this, noting that results release also aims to build a support system of teachers and friends.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my answer earlier, it is something that we continuously review.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Nevertheless, as I mentioned, there are a few things to note when it comes to the release of the results, as we also want to build a support system whereby there are teachers and friends who are available to also support the child.
